children.title: Finite-Precision Momentum Drift
children.top_down_role: Accumulation and persistence of arithmetic error in momentum state.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Momentum Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accumulated roundoff represented as forced momentum dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Model a computed scalar momentum mode by \(\widehat e_{k+1}=a\widehat e_k-\beta\widehat e_{k-1}+\delta_k\), where \(\delta_k\) is the aggregate local floating-point perturbation. Let \(h_{-1}=0\), \(h_0=1\), and \(h_{j+1}=a h_j-\beta h_{j-1}\). Relative to the exact recurrence with identical initial data, the drift is exactly \[\widehat e_k-e_k=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}h_{k-1-i}\delta_i.\] Hence finite-precision effects are accumulated according to the same impulse response that governs momentum transients; small local errors need not remain small when \(\sum_j|h_j|\) is large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Roundoff acts as a forcing term in the momentum recurrence. The resulting drift is the convolution of local errors with the method's impulse response.
assumptions_latex: Each computed update is representable as the exact recurrence plus an additive local error \(\delta_k\).
The computed and exact recurrences start from identical initial states.

notation.meaning: impulse-response sequence of the momentum recurrence

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: variation-of-constants formula for a forced linear recurrence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convolution identity is correct for an assumed additive forced recurrence, but no inspectable source supports interpreting aggregate floating-point effects through this model or its stated numerical implication.

children.title: Transient–Drift Interaction
children.top_down_role: Regimes where prolonged dynamics amplify or conceal finite-precision effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Transient–Drift Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roundoff amplification by repeated-root momentum transients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the forced repeated-root recurrence \[e_{k+1}=2r e_k-r^2e_{k-1}+\delta_k,\qquad |r|<1,\] the impulse response is \(h_j=(j+1)r^j\). Consequently, perturbation-induced drift satisfies \[d_k=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(k-i)r^{k-1-i}\delta_i.\] If \(|\delta_i|\le\varepsilon\), then \(|d_k|\le\varepsilon\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(j+1)|r|^j\le\varepsilon(1-|r|)^{-2}\). Thus a stable but slowly decaying repeated root can amplify persistent numerical drift quadratically in the inverse stability margin, coupling long transients to finite-precision sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a repeated stable root, the same polynomial factor causing long transients also amplifies accumulated perturbations, with a worst-case bound proportional to the inverse squared stability margin.
assumptions_latex: The drift recurrence has zero initial state.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convolution bound for a repeated-root forced recurrence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The repeated-root impulse response and convolution bound are mathematically correct, but the record has no inspectable source supporting its finite-precision interpretation and inverse-stability-margin amplification claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected-gradient form of the Lagrange stationarity condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equates vanishing tangent-space gradient with the multiplier stationarity condition for affine equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathcal C^1(\mathbb R^n)\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, define \(P=I_n-A^\top(AA^\top)^{-1}A\), and let \(x^*\) satisfy \(Ax^*=b\). Then \(P\nabla f(x^*)=0\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(\nabla f(x^*)+A^\top\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point of a smooth affine-equality-constrained problem, the projected gradient vanishes exactly when the Lagrange multiplier stationarity condition holds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected-gradient certificate for affine-constrained convex optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes global minimizers of a differentiable convex function over a full-row-rank affine equality set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and continuously differentiable, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, set \(P=I_n-A^\top(AA^\top)^{-1}A\), and suppose \(Ax^*=b\). Then \(x^*\) is a global minimizer of \(f\) over \(\{x:Ax=b\}\) if and only if \(P\nabla f(x^*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable convex objective and a feasible point of a full-row-rank affine equality set, global optimality is equivalent to a zero projected gradient.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned conjugate-gradient recurrence for an SPD quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard fixed-preconditioner linear PCG; no convergence-rate or finite-termination claim is made by this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=G^T\succ0$ and $W=W^T\succ0$. Given $x_0$, set $g_0=Gx_0+b$, $v_0=W^{-1}g_0$, and $d_0=-v_0$. For $k=0,1,\ldots$ before termination, compute $\alpha_k=\frac{g_k^Tv_k}{d_k^TGd_k}$, $x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k$, $g_{k+1}=g_k+\alpha_kGd_k$, $v_{k+1}=W^{-1}g_{k+1}$, $\beta_k=\frac{g_{k+1}^Tv_{k+1}}{g_k^Tv_k}$, and $d_{k+1}=-v_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the inverse fixed preconditioner to the current residual-gradient, take the corresponding quadratic step, update the point and residual, and combine the new preconditioned residual with the preceding direction using the displayed ratio.
assumptions_latex: g_k\neq0\text{ at each iteration where the displayed quotients are evaluated}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_k,g_k,v_k,d_k)\text{ obey the stated preconditioned conjugate-gradient recurrence for minimizing }\tfrac12x^TGx+b^Tx\text{, equivalently solving }Gx=-b.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal change of variables balancing coordinatewise curvature before fixed-metric gradient iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), choose a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with \(d_i>0\), set \(x=Dz\), and define \(\widetilde f(z)=f(Dz)\). Select \(D\) so that estimated coordinate curvature scales \(c_i>0\) satisfy \(d_i^2c_i\approx 1\), for example \(d_i=c_i^{-1/2}\). Apply gradient descent to \(\widetilde f\): \(z_{k+1}=z_k-\alpha_kD^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(Dz_k)\), and return \(x_k=Dz_k\). Equivalently, \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kDD^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescale variables to balance estimated coordinate curvatures, run gradient descent in the scaled variables, and map iterates back; this is equivalent to fixed diagonal preconditioning.

notation.meaning: estimated curvature scale of coordinate i

children.title: Scaling Quality Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Conditioning and balance indicators used to assess transformed problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Quality Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral and coordinatewise tests for whether a fixed scaling improves smooth-problem geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For twice differentiable \(f\) and nonsingular scaling \(D\), define the scaled Hessian \(H_D(x)=D^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x)D\). On a region \(\Omega\), a scaling-quality certificate consists of constants \(0<\mu_D\le L_D<\infty\) satisfying \(\mu_DI\preceq H_D(x)\preceq L_DI\) for every \(x\in\Omega\). Its spectral diagnostic is \(\kappa_D=L_D/\mu_D\); smaller \(\kappa_D\) predicts a better worst-case linear rate for gradient descent on strongly convex objectives. Coordinate balance may additionally be checked through the spread of \((H_D(x))_{ii}\). These diagnostics are meaningful only relative to the unscaled values or competing scalings on the same region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certify scaling quality by bounding the scaled Hessian, comparing its condition number with alternatives, and checking whether its diagonal curvature scales are balanced.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on a region \(\Omega\).
The scaled Hessian is uniformly positive definite on \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_D=L_D/\mu_D\), with smaller \(\kappa_D\) indicating better-conditioned scaled geometry.

notation.meaning: uniform upper and lower scaled-curvature bounds

children.title: Bounded Metric Sequences
children.top_down_role: Uniformly controlled metric families supporting stable convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Metric Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform spectral control and bounded relative variation for variable metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence of symmetric matrices \((M_k)_{k\ge0}\) is uniformly bounded and coercive if constants \(0<m\le M<\infty\) exist such that \(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\) for every \(k\). A common stronger variable-metric condition requires a summable nonnegative sequence \((\eta_k)\) with \(M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty\). The first condition makes all induced norms uniformly equivalent to the Euclidean norm; the second prevents persistent multiplicative oscillation of the geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable metrics are stable when their eigenvalues stay uniformly away from zero and infinity, with optional summable control of successive metric changes.
assumptions_latex: The matrices act on a fixed finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt m\lVert v\rVert_2\le\lVert v\rVert_{M_k}\le\sqrt M\lVert v\rVert_2\) for all \(v\) and \(k\).

notation.meaning: metric norm defined by the quadratic form

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Curvature Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded diagonal approximations to local curvature for inexpensive variable-metric steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), construct positive coordinate curvature estimates \(c_{k,i}\), for example from diagonal Hessian information or secant ratios when available. Given safeguards \(0<\ell\le u<\infty\), set \(h_{k,i}=\min\{u,\max\{\ell,c_{k,i}\}\}\) and \(H_k=\operatorname{diag}(h_{k,1},\ldots,h_{k,n})\). The unconstrained variable-metric step is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kH_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\). Thus each gradient component is divided by a local curvature surrogate while clipping ensures \(\ell I\preceq H_k\preceq uI\). Stop when a prescribed stationarity test is satisfied and return the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate curvature separately by coordinate, clip the estimates to positive bounds, and divide each gradient component by its safeguarded estimate.
assumptions_latex: The raw curvature estimates \(c_{k,i}\) are finite.

children.title: Metric-Projection Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Projection Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained variable-metric gradient step as a weighted projection or quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(M_k\succ0\). Given \(x_k\in C\) and \(\alpha_k>0\), compute \(y_k=x_k-\alpha_kM_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) and set \(x_{k+1}=P_C^{M_k}(y_k)\), where \(P_C^{M}(y)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\tfrac12\lVert x-y\rVert_M^2\). Equivalently, \(x_{k+1}\) uniquely minimizes \(\langle\nabla f(x_k),x-x_k\rangle+\tfrac{1}{2\alpha_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert_{M_k}^2\) over \(C\). Stop under a prescribed stationarity criterion and return the final feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take a metric-scaled gradient step and project it onto the feasible set in the same metric; equivalently solve a strongly convex local quadratic model.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).

notation.meaning: projection onto the feasible set in metric M

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative-Gradient Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar, diagonal, and full-matrix positive metrics accumulated from past gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For gradients \(g_t\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and regularization \(\delta>0\), cumulative-gradient metrics include the scalar matrix \(H_k^{\mathrm{sc}}=(\delta+\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^k\lVert g_t\rVert_2^2})I\), the diagonal matrix \(H_k^{\mathrm{diag}}=\operatorname{diag}(\delta+\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^kg_{t,1}^2},\ldots,\delta+\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^kg_{t,n}^2})\), and the full matrix \(H_k^{\mathrm{full}}=\delta I+(\sum_{t=1}^kg_tg_t^{\mathsf T})^{1/2}\). Each is positive definite and depends only on gradient history through time \(k\). A metric-scaled step uses \(H_k^{-1}g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative-gradient scaling uses scalar, coordinatewise, or full-matrix square roots of accumulated gradient energy, regularized to remain invertible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed scalar, diagonal, and full-matrix metrics are plausible AdaGrad conventions, but no source is supplied and conventions differ regarding regularization placement and matrix square roots.

children.title: Adaptive-Regularization Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Cumulative scaling viewed through changing regularization geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Regularization Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-scaled updates represented as minimizers of changing quadratic regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_k\succ0\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(\alpha_k>0\). The update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kH_k^{-1}g_k\) is equivalently represented by \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{\langle g_k,x-x_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert_{H_k}^2\right\}.\] When \(H_k\) is formed from cumulative gradients, the regularizer changes with the observed gradient geometry: frequently active directions receive larger quadratic penalties and hence smaller subsequent displacement. The equivalence is exact for each fixed positive-definite \(H_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cumulative-metric gradient step exactly minimizes a linearized objective plus a quadratic regularizer whose geometry adapts to past gradients.

notation.meaning: norm induced by the adaptive metric

children.title: Online AdaGrad Regret-Theory Boundary
children.top_down_role: Navigation boundary for scalar, coordinatewise, and full-matrix adaptive regret guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Online AdaGrad Regret-Theory Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates deterministic smooth descent analysis from adversarial online regret guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For online convex losses \(\ell_t\) on a convex decision set \(C\), regret is \(R_T(u)=\sum_{t=1}^T(\ell_t(x_t)-\ell_t(u))\) for a comparator \(u\in C\). Scalar, diagonal, and full-matrix cumulative-gradient metrics can be analyzed through bounds depending respectively on aggregate, coordinatewise, or directional gradient energy. Such bounds concern a sequence of possibly different losses and comparison with the best fixed decision in hindsight. They do not, without an additional online-to-batch or repeated-objective argument, imply a last-iterate convergence rate for minimizing one smooth deterministic objective. Conversely, deterministic descent estimates do not establish adversarial regret guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AdaGrad regret bounds address changing online losses and fixed-comparator regret; they do not automatically provide last-iterate rates for one deterministic smooth objective.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm chooses \(x_t\) before observing the current loss or subgradient.
The comparator \(u\) is fixed over the horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{online regret guarantee}\not\Rightarrow\text{deterministic last-iterate convergence rate}\) without an explicit transfer argument.

notation.meaning: regret through horizon T relative to comparator u

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The online-versus-deterministic boundary is well framed and the failure_boundary kind fits, but no authoritative online AdaGrad or online-to-batch source is provided.

children.title: Metric Conditioning Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Controls for singular, ill-conditioned, or excessively anisotropic metrics.

children.title: Metric Regularization
children.top_down_role: Controls that prevent singular or severely ill-conditioned metric choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive spectral regularization ensuring invertibility and limiting inverse-step amplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric positive-semidefinite raw metric \(G_k\) and parameter \(\delta_k>0\), form \(M_k=G_k+\delta_kI\). Use the regularized direction \(d_k=-M_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), subject to the method's stopping rule. Since every eigenvalue is shifted by \(\delta_k\), \(M_k\succeq\delta_kI\) and \(\lVert M_k^{-1}\rVert_2\le1/\delta_k\). Thus the metric is invertible even when \(G_k\) is singular, while large \(\delta_k\) moves the direction toward a uniformly scaled negative gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive identity multiple to a semidefinite metric, making it invertible and bounding amplification by its inverse.

children.title: Metric Clipping
children.top_down_role: Bounds limiting extreme coordinate scales or spectral values.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Clipping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral projection of a symmetric metric onto prescribed positive-definite bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric raw metric \(G_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{k,1},\ldots,\lambda_{k,n})Q_k^{\mathsf T}\) and constants \(0<\ell\le u<\infty\), define \(\widehat\lambda_{k,i}=\min\{u,\max\{\ell,\lambda_{k,i}\}\}\) and \(M_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\lambda_{k,1},\ldots,\widehat\lambda_{k,n})Q_k^{\mathsf T}\). Use \(-M_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) as the scaled direction. Then \(\ell I\preceq M_k\preceq uI\) and \(\kappa_2(M_k)\le u/\ell\). For diagonal metrics, the same operation clips each diagonal entry and requires no eigendecomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip every metric eigenvalue to a positive interval, producing a uniformly bounded positive-definite scaling with controlled condition number.

children.title: Metric Safeguard Bias
children.top_down_role: Distortion of curvature adaptation introduced by protective controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Safeguard Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies how regularization or clipping alters the intended preconditioned direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\succ0\) be a raw metric, let \(M\succ0\) be its safeguarded replacement, and let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The directional perturbation is \(e=M^{-1}g-G^{-1}g=(M^{-1}-G^{-1})g=M^{-1}(G-M)G^{-1}g\). Consequently, \(\lVert e\rVert_2\le\lVert M^{-1}\rVert_2\lVert M-G\rVert_2\lVert G^{-1}g\rVert_2\). Thus safeguards stabilize inversion but bias the intended scaled direction whenever they modify the metric. If clipping or regularization becomes inactive asymptotically, this perturbation vanishes provided the displayed factors remain controlled; persistent safeguarding can instead produce persistent directional bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safeguards trade stability for distortion: changing the metric changes its inverse-scaled gradient, with an explicit perturbation bound.

children.title: Metric Representation Families
children.top_down_role: Scalar, diagonal, structured, low-rank, and dense metric formats.

assumptions_latex: Each represented metric is symmetric positive definite; in the structured low-rank case, \(C_k=C_k^{\mathsf T}\) and \(D_k+U_kC_kU_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k=-M_kg_k\) can be computed from any listed representation without changing the abstract variable-metric iteration.

notation.meaning: positive-definite scaling metric at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical finite-dimensional matrix representations used by variable-metric methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite-dimensional representations of positive-definite scaling metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge1\), a symmetric positive-definite metric \(M_k\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) used in the scaled direction \(d_k=-M_kg_k\) may be represented densely by storing its independent entries; diagonally as \(M_k=\operatorname{diag}(m_k)\) with \(m_k\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\); scalarly as \(M_k=\gamma_kI\) with \(\gamma_k>0\); in structured low-rank form as \(M_k=D_k+U_kC_kU_k^{\mathsf T}\), where \(D_k\) is positive diagonal, \(U_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), \(C_k=C_k^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\), and the resulting sum is positive definite; or implicitly in limited-memory form, where \(M_kg_k\) is computed from at most \(m\) stored vector pairs without forming \(M_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite scaling metric may be represented densely, diagonally, as a scalar identity multiple, by positive-definite structured low-rank data, or implicitly using limited-memory vector pairs.

children.title: Metric Update Costs
children.top_down_role: Computational expense associated with refreshing changing metrics.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Update Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic costs for refreshing common metric representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the unit-cost real-arithmetic model, refreshing every stored parameter of an \(n\)-dimensional metric has cost \(\Theta(n^2)\) for an unstructured dense matrix, \(\Theta(n)\) for a diagonal metric, and \(\Theta(1)\) for a scalar multiple of the identity. Updating an explicitly stored rank-\(r\) factor \(U_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) costs \(\Theta(nr)\) when all factor entries are refreshed. Appending one curvature pair to a limited-memory representation costs \(\Theta(n)\), excluding gradient evaluation and any separate line search; maintaining at most \(m\) pairs does not alter this per-pair insertion order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense metrics cost quadratic time to refresh; diagonal and limited-memory pair updates cost linear time; scalar updates cost constant time.
assumptions_latex: Each scalar read, write, and arithmetic operation has unit cost.
A refresh touches every explicitly stored parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update costs are \(\Theta(n^2)\), \(\Theta(n)\), \(\Theta(1)\), \(\Theta(nr)\), and \(\Theta(n)\) for dense, diagonal, scalar, rank-\(r\), and pair-appending representations, respectively.

notation.meaning: maximum number of stored curvature pairs

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operation counts follow the number of refreshed representation parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits Metric Update Costs and the operation counts are coherent under the stated full-refresh unit-cost model. No inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Metric Storage Costs
children.top_down_role: Memory requirements associated with alternative metric formats.

assumptions_latex: Only representation data are counted; objective data and workspace storage are excluded.
The limited-memory capacity reserves storage for exactly \(m\) vector pairs and at most \(O(m)\) associated scalars.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The storage capacities scale as \(\Theta(n^2)\), \(\Theta(n)\), \(\Theta(1)\), \(\Theta(nr+r^2)\), and \(\Theta(mn)\) for the five respective families.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: storage counts follow directly from explicitly listed scalar parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage requirements for common finite-dimensional metric representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Counting real scalars, an unstructured symmetric \(n\times n\) metric requires \(n(n+1)/2=\Theta(n^2)\) storage, a diagonal metric requires \(n=\Theta(n)\), and a scalar metric requires \(1=\Theta(1)\). A representation \(D_k+U_kC_kU_k^{\mathsf T}\), with diagonal \(D_k\), \(U_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), and dense symmetric \(C_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\), requires \(n+nr+r(r+1)/2=\Theta(nr+r^2)\) scalars. Capacity for exactly \(m\) curvature pairs in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), together with at most \(O(m)\) associated scalars, requires \(2mn+O(m)=\Theta(mn)\) scalars.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense storage is quadratic, diagonal storage linear, scalar storage constant, low-rank storage depends on dimension and rank, and capacity for a fixed number of limited-memory pairs is proportional to memory depth times dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric Storage Costs

children.title: Structure–Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between curvature expressiveness and implementation expense.

assumptions_latex: The same target pair \((H,g)\) is used for both families.
Storage and arithmetic are compared using the explicit representation and unit-cost models stated in the prerequisite cost records.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e(\mathcal{M}_2;H,g)\le e(\mathcal{M}_1;H,g)\); any accompanying increase in computational cost must be assessed from the representations used for the two families.

notation.meaning: best directional approximation error over a metric family

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: approximation monotonicity follows from minimization over nested sets; representation costs require an explicit cost model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation and computational tradeoffs induced by restricting the metric representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{M}_1\subseteq\mathcal{M}_2\subseteq\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), and for \(H\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) and \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) define \(e(\mathcal{M};H,g)=\inf_{M\in\mathcal{M}}\lVert(M-H)g\rVert_2\). Then \(e(\mathcal{M}_2;H,g)\le e(\mathcal{M}_1;H,g)\). Thus enlarging the admissible family cannot worsen the best attainable scaled-direction fit. When the larger family is implemented with additional dense entries, factor columns, or stored vector pairs, its storage and arithmetic costs are those of that richer representation and may exceed the costs of a scalar, diagonal, lower-rank, or shorter-memory implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger admissible metric family cannot have worse best directional approximation error. Its computational cost may be higher when its implementation stores or updates more representation data.

children.title: Quadratic Conjugate-Direction Model

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Conjugate-Direction Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear conjugate-gradient template for a strictly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), minimize \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\). Set \(g_0=Ax_0-b\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). While \(g_k\ne0\), compute \(\alpha_k=-g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k/(d_k^{\mathsf T}Ad_k)\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), \(g_{k+1}=Ax_{k+1}-b\), \(\beta_{k+1}=\|g_{k+1}\|_2^2/\|g_k\|_2^2\), and \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\). Stop when \(g_k=0\) and output \(x_k\); in exact arithmetic this occurs within at most \(n\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear conjugate gradient minimizes a positive-definite quadratic using exact line searches and mutually conjugate directions, terminating within the dimension in exact arithmetic.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic and matrix-vector products are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output equals \(x_\star=A^{-1}b\), and nonzero generated directions satisfy \(d_i^{\mathsf T}Ad_j=0\) for \(i\ne j\).

notation.meaning: quadratic gradient at the kth iterate

children.title: Nonlinear Direction-Recurrence Framework
children.top_down_role: The common structural organizer for nonlinear conjugate-gradient updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Direction-Recurrence Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared recurrence underlying standard nonlinear conjugate-gradient methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For continuously differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), choose \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), and set \(d_0=-g_0\). At iteration \(k\), choose a positive line-search step \(\alpha_k\), update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), evaluate \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\), select a method-specific coefficient \(\beta_{k+1}\), and set \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\). Stop when a prescribed condition such as \(\|g_k\|_2\le\varepsilon\) holds; otherwise output the final iterate after the allowed iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear conjugate-gradient methods share a gradient-plus-previous-direction recurrence and differ mainly in their coefficient and line-search safeguards.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every standard nonlinear conjugate-gradient variant is obtained by specifying \(\beta_{k+1}\), the line search, and any restart or truncation rule in this recurrence.

children.title: Exact-Search Quadratic Equivalences
children.top_down_role: Coincidences among update families in the ideal quadratic regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Search Quadratic Equivalences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient coincidences for exact line search on a positive-definite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), and generate \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\) using exact minimization of \(f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\). Before termination, the gradients are mutually orthogonal and successive directions are \(A\)-conjugate. Consequently, whenever their denominators are nonzero, the Fletcher–Reeves, Polak–Ribiere–Polyak, Hestenes–Stiefel, Dai–Yuan, and Hager–Zhang formulas produce the same \(\beta_{k+1}\) as linear conjugate gradient. Hence all five recurrences generate identical iterates and directions in exact arithmetic from the same \(x_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a positive-definite quadratic with exact line searches, the principal nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficients coincide with linear conjugate gradient.
assumptions_latex: Every line search is exact and arithmetic is exact.
All displayed coefficient denominators are nonzero before termination.

notation.meaning: gradient of the quadratic at the kth iterate

children.title: Fletcher-Reeves Family
children.top_down_role: Norm-ratio nonlinear conjugate-gradient variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Fletcher-Reeves Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-ratio nonlinear conjugate-gradient update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within the nonlinear recurrence, define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), choose \(d_0=-g_0\), and after obtaining \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), set \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{FR}}=\|g_{k+1}\|_2^2/\|g_k\|_2^2\) whenever \(g_k\ne0\). Then set \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{FR}}d_k\). A restarted Fletcher–Reeves member replaces this coefficient by zero when its prescribed restart test fires. Stop and output \(x_k\) when \(\|g_k\|_2\le\varepsilon\), or after the iteration budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fletcher–Reeves scales the previous direction by the ratio of successive squared gradient norms, optionally resetting that coefficient at restarts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next direction is \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+(\|g_{k+1}\|_2^2/\|g_k\|_2^2)d_k\), unless a restart sets the coefficient to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Fletcher–Reeves norm-ratio coefficient and records its reduction from Polak–Ribière under successive-gradient orthogonality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \((g^{(k)})^\top g^{(k)}\neq0\), the Fletcher–Reeves coefficient is
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}=\frac{(g^{(k+1)})^\top g^{(k+1)}}{(g^{(k)})^\top g^{(k)}}.
\]
When \((g^{(k+1)})^\top g^{(k)}=0\), the Polak–Ribière numerator satisfies
\[
(g^{(k+1)})^\top(g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)})=(g^{(k+1)})^\top g^{(k+1)},
\]
so the Polak–Ribière coefficient reduces to the Fletcher–Reeves coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fletcher–Reeves coefficient is the ratio of the squared norms of two successive gradients. If successive gradients are orthogonal, the Polak–Ribière formula reduces to this ratio.

children.title: Polak-Ribiere-Polyak Family
children.top_down_role: Gradient-difference variants and restart-compatible modifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Polak-Ribiere-Polyak Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient-difference update and its nonnegative truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and \(d_0=-g_0\). After a positive line-search step, define \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PRP}}=g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k/\|g_k\|_2^2\) when \(g_k\ne0\), and set \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PRP}}d_k\). The PRP-plus modification uses \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PRP+}}=\max\{0,\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PRP}}\}\), thereby restarting to steepest descent whenever the untruncated coefficient is negative. Stop at \(\|g_k\|_2\le\varepsilon\) or the iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PRP uses the new gradient paired with the gradient difference; PRP-plus truncates negative coefficients to trigger a steepest-descent restart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: PRP and PRP-plus use the same recurrence, with coefficients \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k/\|g_k\|_2^2\) and \(\max\{0,g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k/\|g_k\|_2^2\}\), respectively.

knowledge_statements.title: Hestenes-Stiefel Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-curvature-scaled nonlinear conjugate-gradient update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and \(d_0=-g_0\). After obtaining \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), define \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HS}}=g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k/(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)\) whenever \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\ne0\), and set \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HS}}d_k\). Safeguarded members may truncate or restart this coefficient when the denominator is too small or the resulting direction fails a prescribed descent test. Stop at the gradient tolerance or iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hestenes–Stiefel divides a gradient-difference numerator by directional curvature, with safeguards or restarts when curvature is unreliable.
assumptions_latex: \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\ne0\) whenever the raw coefficient is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The raw update is \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k/(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k))d_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and raw Hestenes-Stiefel coefficient are mathematically standard and locally consistent, but no citation with an inspectable locator is supplied for either the formula or the described safeguards.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hestenes–Stiefel nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Hestenes–Stiefel update and records the quadratic gradient-difference identity motivating it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g^{(j)}=\nabla f(x^{(j)})\) and \(x^{(k+1)}=x^{(k)}+\alpha_k d^{(k)}\). If \((d^{(k)})^\top(g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)})\neq0\), the Hestenes–Stiefel coefficient is
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}=\frac{(g^{(k+1)})^\top(g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)})}{(d^{(k)})^\top(g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)})}.
\]
For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx-b^\top x+c\), one has \(g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)}=\alpha_kQd^{(k)}\), so this formula is obtained from the quadratic conjugate-direction coefficient by substituting \(Qd^{(k)}=(g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)})/\alpha_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For successive gradients and a nonzero denominator, the Hestenes–Stiefel coefficient is the inner product of the new gradient with the gradient difference divided by the inner product of the current direction with that difference. For a quadratic objective, the gradient difference equals the step length times Q applied to the current direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Hager-Zhang Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hager–Zhang update with a sufficient-descent safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and suppose \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\ne0\). Define \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HZ}}=((y_k-2d_k\|y_k\|_2^2/(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k))^{\mathsf T}g_{k+1})/(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)\). A safeguarded Hager–Zhang update sets \(\beta_{k+1}=\max\{\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HZ}},\eta_k\}\), where \(\eta_k=-1/(\|d_k\|_2\min\{\eta,\|g_k\|_2\})\) for fixed \(\eta>0\), and then uses \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\). The line search and safeguard are chosen to maintain sufficient descent; stop at the gradient tolerance or iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hager–Zhang combines a gradient-difference coefficient with a lower safeguard designed to preserve sufficiently descending directions under compatible line searches.

children.title: Hybrid Conjugate-Gradient Coefficients
children.top_down_role: Combinations that switch or blend established nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Conjugate-Gradient Coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic safeguarded hybridization of two nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(y_{k-1}=g_k-g_{k-1}\). Given two defined base coefficients \(\beta_k^{(1)}\) and \(\beta_k^{(2)}\), a hybrid coefficient is \[\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}=\Pi_{[\ell_k,u_k]}\!\left((1-\lambda_k)\beta_k^{(1)}+\lambda_k\beta_k^{(2)}\right),\qquad 0\leq\lambda_k\leq1,\] where \(\ell_k\leq u_k\) and \(\Pi_{[\ell_k,u_k]}(t)=\min\{u_k,\max\{\ell_k,t\}\}\). The associated direction is \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}d_{k-1}\), with \(d_0=-g_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid coefficient is a safeguarded convex combination of two admissible conjugate-gradient coefficients, used in the standard two-term search-direction recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}d_{k-1}\) defines the corresponding safeguarded hybrid direction.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection of a scalar onto an interval.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the coefficient leaf, but the safeguarded convex-combination formula is only a generic construction and is not tied to an identified hybrid conjugate-gradient family. The plain statement additionally calls the base coefficients admissible, whereas the mathematical statement assumes only that they are defined.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Conjugate-Gradient Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar-parameter family interpolating nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose a line-search step \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and compute \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\). For prescribed endpoint formulas \(B_{k+1}^{(0)}\) and \(B_{k+1}^{(1)}\), choose \(\tau_{k+1}\in[0,1]\) and define \[\beta_{k+1}(\tau_{k+1})=(1-\tau_{k+1})B_{k+1}^{(0)}+\tau_{k+1}B_{k+1}^{(1)},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}(\tau_{k+1})d_k.\] Stop when a specified gradient-norm tolerance is met; otherwise output the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family interpolates between two conjugate-gradient coefficient formulas through a scalar parameter and inserts the result into the usual direction recurrence.
assumptions_latex: The endpoint coefficients are defined whenever used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure generates a parameterized family of nonlinear conjugate-gradient iterates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate kind, but unspecified endpoint formulas make this an arbitrary interpolation template rather than a source-supported parameterized conjugate-gradient family.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterationwise rules selecting between or blending candidate conjugate-gradient coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta_k^{(1)}\) and \(\beta_k^{(2)}\) be candidate coefficients and let \(D_k\subset\mathbb{R}\) be the set of coefficients satisfying the required safeguards at iteration \(k\), such as descent or boundedness tests. A hybrid selection regime chooses \[\beta_k\in D_k\cap\operatorname{conv}\{\beta_k^{(1)},\beta_k^{(2)}\}.\] Endpoint switching selects one candidate lying in \(D_k\); clipped blending selects \(\Pi_{D_k}((1-\lambda_k)\beta_k^{(1)}+\lambda_k\beta_k^{(2)})\) when \(D_k\) is a nonempty closed interval. If the intersection is empty, the regime restarts by setting \(\beta_k=0\), hence \(d_k=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid regime selects a safeguarded endpoint or blend of candidate coefficients and restarts with steepest descent when no candidate is admissible.
assumptions_latex: The two candidate coefficients are finite
\(D_k\) is specified by the method's safeguards
Projection is used only when \(D_k\) is a nonempty closed interval
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected coefficient is admissible whenever the feasible intersection is nonempty; otherwise the rule produces a restart.

notation.meaning: Admissible coefficient set at iteration k.
Scalar projection onto the admissible interval.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the leaf, but the clipped projection onto D_k need not remain in the convex hull of the two coefficients, so it does not necessarily satisfy the initially stated selection rule. A family-specific source and corrected regime are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Modified Conjugate-Gradient Recurrences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic two-term recurrence augmented by a controlled correction vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and compute \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\). Select a conjugate-gradient coefficient \(\beta_{k+1}\), a correction vector \(v_{k+1}\), and a modification parameter \(\eta_{k+1}\), then update \[d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k+\eta_{k+1}v_{k+1}.\] Accept the direction only if \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k+1}<0\); otherwise restart with \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\). Stop at the prescribed gradient tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modified recurrence adds a controlled correction vector to the ordinary conjugate-gradient direction and restarts whenever descent is lost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted or restarted direction satisfies \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k+1}<0\) when \(g_{k+1}\neq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the recurrence leaf, but the arbitrary correction vector and weight do not identify the intended modified conjugate-gradient family. The displayed recurrence requires a source specifying these quantities.

children.title: Accelerated Conjugate-Gradient Variants

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Conjugate-Gradient Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extrapolated nonlinear conjugate-gradient template with a safeguarded direction recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0=x_{-1}\in\mathbb{R}^n\), choose \(t_0=1\), and set \(d_{-1}=0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose an extrapolation factor \(\theta_k\), form \(z_k=x_k+\theta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\), and set \(g_k=\nabla f(z_k)\). Compute \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\), replacing it by \(-g_k\) unless \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\). Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by line search from \(z_k\), set \(x_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and update the acceleration state, for example \(t_{k+1}=(1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2})/2\) and \(\theta_{k+1}=(t_k-1)/t_{k+1}\). Stop at the prescribed stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accelerated variant extrapolates the iterate before forming a safeguarded conjugate-gradient direction and taking a line-search step.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient \(\beta_k\) is defined at each iteration
The line search returns a positive step
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The template produces extrapolated iterates with descent directions at each accepted line-search call.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the variants leaf, but combining a Nesterov-style state update with a nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence is family-specific and unsupported here. The coefficient and admissible extrapolation regime are also unspecified.

children.title: Modification Robustness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Curvature and line-search regimes where modified recurrences lose their intended benefit.

knowledge_statements.title: Modification Robustness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp iterationwise descent boundary for additive direction modifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the unmodified direction \(p_k\) satisfy \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k\leq-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\) for some \(c>0\), and let the modified direction be \(d_k=p_k+e_k\). If \(\lVert e_k\rVert\leq\rho\lVert g_k\rVert\) with \(0\leq\rho<c\), then \[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-(c-\rho)\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\qquad\text{whenever }g_k\neq0.\] The threshold is sharp under only this norm bound: when \(\rho\geq c\), choosing \(p_k=-c g_k\) and \(e_k=\rho g_k\) yields \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=(\rho-c)\lVert g_k\rVert^2\geq0\), so descent may fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive modification preserves sufficient descent when its relative norm is below the descent margin; at or above that margin, a parallel perturbation can destroy descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Descent is guaranteed for \(\rho<c\) and is not guaranteed for \(\rho\geq c\).

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Term Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions with two carried vector components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and define \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\) and \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\). Select scalar coefficients \(\beta_{k+1}\) and \(\gamma_{k+1}\), then form the three-term direction \[d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k+\gamma_{k+1}y_k.\] If a prescribed descent safeguard fails, set \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\). Stop when \(\lVert g_k\rVert\) meets the requested tolerance and output \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three-term nonlinear conjugate gradient augments the negative gradient and previous direction with a third component, commonly the gradient difference.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient formulas are defined whenever used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence generates directions containing the additional component \(y_k\), with restart available to enforce descent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate directions with respect to an SPD matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of pairwise A-conjugacy together with its immediate independence property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} be symmetric positive definite. Nonzero vectors \{p_0,\ldots,p_\ell\} are conjugate with respect to A if p_i^TAp_j=0 for every i\ne j. Every such set is linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonzero vectors are conjugate with respect to a symmetric positive-definite matrix A when every distinct pair is orthogonal in the A inner product. Any A-conjugate set is linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall i\ne j,\ p_i^TAp_j=0\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \{p_0,\ldots,p_\ell\}\text{ is linearly independent}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate directions for a diagonal SPD quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal case illustrating conjugate directions as transformed coordinate search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If A=\operatorname{diag}(a_1,\ldots,a_n) with a_i>0 and \phi(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx-b^Tx, then the coordinate vectors e_1,\ldots,e_n are A-conjugate. Consequently, exact one-dimensional minimization successively along the coordinate directions attains the unique minimizer of \phi after at most one minimization per coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive diagonal quadratic, the coordinate axes are mutually A-conjugate. Exact minimization once along each coordinate direction therefore finds the quadratic's unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_i^TAe_j=0\ \forall i\ne j,\qquad \text{successive exact coordinate minimizations attain }\operatorname*{argmin}\phi.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate-direction coordinates diagonalize the quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis transformation interpreting conjugate-direction minimization as coordinate minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A=A^T\succ0 and let \{p_0,\ldots,p_{n-1}\} be nonzero A-conjugate directions. With S=[p_0\ p_1\ \cdots\ p_{n-1}], the matrix S is nonsingular and S^TAS is diagonal. Under x=S\hat{x}, the quadratic \phi(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx-b^Tx becomes \hat\phi(\hat{x})=\tfrac12\hat{x}^T(S^TAS)\hat{x}-(S^Tb)^T\hat{x}. Exact coordinate minimization of \hat\phi is equivalent to the conjugate-direction iteration in x-space and terminates in at most n steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete A-conjugate set forms a basis in which the SPD quadratic has a diagonal Hessian. Coordinate minimization in the transformed variables is exactly conjugate-direction minimization in the original variables and reaches the minimizer in at most n steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is nonsingular},\quad S^TAS\text{ is diagonal},\quad \hat\phi(\hat{x})=\tfrac12\hat{x}^T(S^TAS)\hat{x}-(S^Tb)^T\hat{x},\quad \text{and transformed coordinate search terminates in at most }n\text{ steps}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-line-search conjugate-direction iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration for a strictly convex quadratic when a complete A-conjugate direction set is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given A=A^T\succ0, b\in\mathbb{R}^n, \phi(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx-b^Tx, x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n, and A-conjugate directions \{p_0,\ldots,p_{n-1}\}, define r_k=Ax_k-b and, for k=0,\ldots,n-1, set \alpha_k=-\frac{r_k^Tp_k}{p_k^TAp_k},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k. Then \alpha_k is the unique minimizer of \alpha\mapsto\phi(x_k+\alpha p_k).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from any point and a complete set of A-conjugate directions, update along each direction using minus the residual-direction inner product divided by the direction's A-norm squared. This step length uniquely minimizes the quadratic along that line.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Roles and practical characteristics of conjugate-gradient methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A method-family characterization rather than a convergence theorem; the performance comparison with steepest descent is qualitative and carries no stated rate or universal quantifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear system $Ax=b$ with $A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0$, linear conjugate gradient is an iterative alternative to Gaussian elimination suited to large problems. Its performance depends on the eigenvalue distribution of $A$, and preconditioning can make that distribution more favorable and thereby improve convergence significantly. Nonlinear conjugate-gradient extensions are designed for large-scale nonlinear optimization, require no matrix storage, and are characterized in the extract as faster than steepest descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear system whose coefficient matrix is symmetric positive definite, linear conjugate gradient is an iterative alternative to Gaussian elimination suited to large problems. Its performance depends on the matrix's eigenvalue distribution, and preconditioning can improve that distribution and hence convergence. Nonlinear conjugate-gradient extensions target large-scale nonlinear optimization, require no matrix storage, and are qualitatively described as faster than steepest descent.
assumptions_latex: \text{No explicit smoothness, line-search, or convexity assumptions are stated for the nonlinear claim}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{performance}(\mathrm{CG},A)\ \text{depends on}\ \sigma(A),\qquad \text{and suitable preconditioning can improve the spectral distribution and convergence; nonlinear CG provides matrix-free large-scale optimization extensions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite termination of the conjugate-direction method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic termination for a complete set of conjugate directions on an SPD system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} be symmetric positive definite, b\in\mathbb{R}^n, and let \{p_0,\ldots,p_{n-1}\} be nonzero A-conjugate directions. For any x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n, define r_k=Ax_k-b, \alpha_k=-\frac{r_k^Tp_k}{p_k^TAp_k}, and x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k. Then the sequence reaches the unique solution x^*=A^{-1}b in at most n steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any starting point, exact line minimization successively along a complete set of A-conjugate directions reaches the unique solution of an SPD linear system after at most n updates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned linear conjugate-gradient iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm for solving a symmetric positive-definite linear system using a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner; no convergence-rate claim is asserted here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the system $Ax=b$, let $A\succ0$, choose $x_0$, set $r_0=Ax_0-b$, solve $My_0=r_0$, and set $p_0=-y_0$. While $r_k\ne0$, compute
\[
\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^Ty_k}{p_k^TAp_k},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\qquad r_{k+1}=r_k+\alpha_kAp_k,
\]
solve $My_{k+1}=r_{k+1}$, and set
\[
\beta_{k+1}=\frac{r_{k+1}^Ty_{k+1}}{r_k^Ty_k},\qquad p_{k+1}=-y_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k.
\]
Terminate when $r_k=0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To solve Ax=b, form the residual, apply the preconditioner by solving My=r, and initialize the search direction as minus the preconditioned residual. At each nonzero residual, compute the conjugate-gradient step length, update the iterate and residual, apply the preconditioner again, and form the next direction from the new preconditioned residual and the preceding direction. Stop when the residual is zero.
assumptions_latex: My_k=r_k\text{ is solved at each iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_k=0\ \Longrightarrow\ Ax_k=b\text{ and the iteration terminates at }x_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient with Polak–Ribière Update and Restarts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained nonlinear conjugate-gradient iteration under exact line minimization, including its descent identity and the loss-of-conjugacy boundary motivating restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable. Set $d^0=-\nabla f(x^0)$ and, for $k\ge1$, use
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha^kd^k,\qquad \alpha^k\in\arg\min_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}}f(x^k+\alpha d^k),
\]
\[
d^k=-\nabla f(x^k)+\beta^kd^{k-1},\qquad
\beta^k=\frac{\nabla f(x^k)^T\bigl(\nabla f(x^k)-\nabla f(x^{k-1})\bigr)}{\|\nabla f(x^{k-1})\|_2^2}.
\]
Exact line minimization at the preceding step gives $\nabla f(x^k)^Td^{k-1}=0$, and therefore
\[
\nabla f(x^k)^Td^k=-\|\nabla f(x^k)\|_2^2.
\]
Thus $d^k$ is a strict descent direction whenever $\nabla f(x^k)\ne0$. Because nonquadratic terms or inaccurate line searches can destroy conjugacy, a cycle may be restarted with $d^k=-\nabla f(x^k)$ periodically or when
\[
|\nabla f(x^k)^T\nabla f(x^{k-1})|>\gamma\|\nabla f(x^{k-1})\|_2^2,\qquad 0<\gamma<1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear conjugate gradient starts from steepest descent and then uses the Polak–Ribière two-term direction update. Under exact line minimization, the current gradient is orthogonal to the preceding direction, so the new direction has gradient inner product equal to minus the squared gradient norm and is strictly descending away from stationarity. Nonquadratic curvature or inaccurate line searches can destroy conjugacy and invalidate that exact identity, motivating periodic or orthogonality-test restarts to steepest descent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial optimality of the conjugate-gradient iterate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard quadratic-energy notation implicit in the extracted conjugate-gradient theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf Q=\mathbf Q^T\succ0\), let \(\mathbf x^*\) minimize the associated quadratic, and define \(E(\mathbf x)=\tfrac12(\mathbf x-\mathbf x^*)^T\mathbf Q(\mathbf x-\mathbf x^*)\). If \(\mathbf x_{k+1}\) is generated by conjugate gradient and \(\mathcal P_k\) denotes the polynomials of degree at most \(k\), then

\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Krylov-span and conjugacy identities for conjugate gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic structural identities for classical CG before termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=Q^T\succ0\), let \(g_k=Qx_k-b\), and generate \(x_k,d_k,\alpha_k,\beta_k\) by the classical conjugate-gradient recurrence. If the method has not terminated at \(x_k\), then \[\operatorname{span}\{g_0,\ldots,g_k\}=\operatorname{span}\{g_0,Qg_0,\ldots,Q^kg_0\},\] \[\operatorname{span}\{d_0,\ldots,d_k\}=\operatorname{span}\{g_0,Qg_0,\ldots,Q^kg_0\},\] \[d_k^TQd_i=0\quad(0\le i<k),\] and the coefficients admit the identities \[\alpha_k=\frac{g_k^Tg_k}{d_k^TQd_k},\qquad \beta_k=\frac{g_{k+1}^Tg_{k+1}}{g_k^Tg_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before termination, the gradients and search directions generated by classical CG span the same Krylov subspace. The directions are pairwise conjugate with respect to Q, and the step and direction-update coefficients have the stated squared-gradient formulas.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-line-search and restart logic in Beale’s three-term CG method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation fragment of Beale’s method. The cited three-term formulas defining $d_k$ are not reproduced in this extract, so the statement records them as the prescribed Beale recurrence without reconstructing them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration $k$, choose $\alpha_k$ by exact line search, set $x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k$, increment $k$, and evaluate $g_k=\nabla f(x_k)$. Terminate if $\|g_k\|\le\epsilon$. Otherwise, if $|g_{k-1}^{T}g_k|\ge0.2\|g_k\|^2$ and $k-t\ge n-1$, reset $t=k-1$; then compute $d_k$ by the prescribed Beale three-term recurrence. When $k>t+1$, accept the direction only if $-1.2\|g_k\|^2\le d_k^Tg_k\le-0.8\|g_k\|^2$; if this test fails, reset $t=k-1$ and recompute the direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use exact line search, update the point, and stop when the new gradient meets the tolerance. A loss-of-orthogonality/elapsed-iteration test can reset the reference counter. After forming the prescribed three-term direction, iterations beyond the first post-reset step require its directional derivative to lie between minus 1.2 and minus 0.8 times the squared gradient norm; otherwise the method restarts and recomputes the direction.
assumptions_latex: d_k\text{ is computed by the prescribed Beale three-term recurrence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|g_k\|\le\epsilon\Rightarrow\text{terminate};\quad k>t+1\text{ and }d_k^Tg_k\notin[-1.2\|g_k\|^2,-0.8\|g_k\|^2]\Rightarrow t\leftarrow k-1\text{ and the direction is recomputed}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classical conjugate-gradient algorithm for a positive-definite quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic recurrence for minimizing a strictly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx-b^Tx\) with \(Q=Q^T\succ0\), and choose any \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\). Set \(g_k=Qx_k-b\) and \(d_0=-g_0=b-Qx_0\). While \(g_k\neq0\), compute \[\alpha_k=-\frac{g_k^Td_k}{d_k^TQd_k},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\] \[\beta_k=\frac{g_{k+1}^TQd_k}{d_k^TQd_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.\] The first iteration is a steepest-descent step; subsequent directions combine the current negative gradient with the preceding direction. In exact arithmetic the iteration terminates after finitely many steps at the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric positive-definite quadratic, start with the negative gradient, perform the stated exact line-search step, and update each new direction from the new negative gradient plus a multiple of the previous direction. The first step is steepest descent, and exact-arithmetic CG reaches the minimizer in finitely many iterations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Beale's three-term cycle recurrence, its exact-quadratic conjugacy and affine-subspace properties, and the explicit failure boundary that the generated direction need not be descending even with exact line searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(y_j=g_{j+1}-g_j\). For a conjugate-gradient cycle restarted at iteration \(t\), first set \[d_{t+1}=-g_{t+1}+\beta_td_t.\] For \(t+2\le k\le t+n-1\), Beale's reduced three-term recurrence is \[d_k=-g_k+\beta_{k-1}d_{k-1}+\gamma_{k-1}d_t,\] with \[\beta_{k-1}=\frac{g_k^Ty_{k-1}}{d_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1}},\qquad \gamma_{k-1}=\frac{g_k^Ty_t}{d_t^Ty_t}.\] Under the stated quadratic exact-line-search conjugacy relations, the intermediate coefficients in the unreduced recurrence vanish, and equivalent exact-quadratic CG formulas, including Fletcher--Reeves, may be used for \(\beta_{k-1}\). Moreover, \[\mathcal B_{k-1}=x_t+\operatorname{span}\{d_t,\ldots,d_{k-1}\}=x_t+\operatorname{span}\{d_t,g_{t+1},\ldots,g_{k-1}\},\] and if \(x_k\) minimizes the quadratic over \(\mathcal B_{k-1}\), then \[g_k\perp\operatorname{span}\{d_t,\ldots,d_{k-1}\},\qquad g_k\perp\operatorname{span}\{d_t,g_{t+1},\ldots,g_{k-1}\}.\] The recurrence does not guarantee \(g_k^Td_k<0\), even with exact line searches. The extract proposes the controls \[-g_k^Td_k\ge\sigma\|g_k\|\|d_k\|\quad(\sigma>0),\qquad |g_{k-1}^Tg_k|<0.2\|g_k\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a cycle restarted at t, Beale's method combines the negative current gradient, the preceding direction, and the direction retained from the cycle start. Under exact quadratic conjugacy, the full recurrence reduces to these three terms, and minimization over the cycle's affine space makes the new gradient orthogonal to the corresponding direction and gradient spans. The recurrence can nevertheless produce a non-descent direction even with exact line searches, motivating sufficient-descent and near-orthogonality controls.
assumptions_latex: t+2\le k\le t+n-1\text{ for the displayed three-term recurrence}
f(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx+b^Tx+c\text{ with symmetric positive-definite }G\text{ for the exact-quadratic conjugacy and affine-minimization conclusions}
d_j^TGd_i=0\text{ for the required cycle direction pairs}
\text{line searches are exact for the stated coefficient equivalences and orthogonality properties}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate-gradient direction construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction construction and termination geometry for the classical quadratic conjugate-gradient method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a quadratic problem with conjugacy induced by \(Q\), conjugate gradient constructs \(d_k\) sequentially by adding to \(-g_k\) a linear combination of preceding directions so that \(d_k\) is \(Q\)-conjugate to them. If the solution has not yet been attained, then \(g_k\neq 0\), \(g_k\perp \mathcal B_k:=\operatorname{span}\{d_0,\ldots,d_{k-1}\}\), and \(g_k\) is linearly independent of the preceding directions. If the solution is attained before \(n\) steps, then \(g_k=0\) and the process terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate gradient forms each direction sequentially from the current negative gradient and earlier directions, enforcing conjugacy. Before termination, the current gradient is nonzero and orthogonal to the span of all earlier directions; upon reaching the solution, the gradient vanishes and the method stops.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_k\perp\mathcal B_k\text{ before termination},\qquad g_k=0\text{ at early termination}.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear conjugate gradient with a positive scalar scaling of the gradient component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), choose \(\sigma_0>0\), and let \(d_0=-\sigma_0g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by line search, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and compute \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\). Choose a scale \(\sigma_{k+1}>0\) and a conjugate-gradient coefficient \(\beta_{k+1}\), then set \[d_{k+1}=-\sigma_{k+1}g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k.\] Restart with \(d_{k+1}=-\sigma_{k+1}g_{k+1}\) if the proposed direction fails the selected descent test; stop at the prescribed gradient tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled nonlinear conjugate gradient multiplies the negative-gradient component by a positive iteration-dependent scalar while retaining the conjugate-gradient memory term.
assumptions_latex: The line search returns a positive step
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method generates scaled nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions and can restart to a scaled steepest-descent direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed positive-definite preconditioning applied to nonlinear conjugate-gradient residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. Given \(x_0\), compute \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), solve \(Mz_0=g_0\), and set \(d_0=-z_0\). After choosing \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), compute \(g_{k+1}\), and solve \(Mz_{k+1}=g_{k+1}\). One preconditioned Polak--Ribiere recurrence is \[\beta_{k+1}=\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}(z_{k+1}-z_k)}{g_k^{\mathsf T}z_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=-z_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k.\] Restart with \(-z_{k+1}\) when the denominator vanishes or the direction fails the prescribed descent test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned nonlinear conjugate gradient replaces the raw gradient by the solution of a positive-definite preconditioning system and uses it in the recurrence.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient is used only when \(g_k^{\mathsf T}z_k>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence defines a fixed-metric preconditioned nonlinear conjugate-gradient method.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned conjugate-gradient iteration for an SPD quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PCG recurrences for minimizing a symmetric positive-definite quadratic using a fixed symmetric positive-definite preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0 and M=M^{\mathsf T}\succ0. Given x_0, set g_0=Hx_0+c, v_0=M^{-1}g_0, and p_0=-v_0. For each performed iteration k, set \alpha_k=\frac{\langle g_k,v_k\rangle}{\langle p_k,Hp_k\rangle},\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\quad g_{k+1}=g_k+\alpha_kHp_k,\quad v_{k+1}=M^{-1}g_{k+1},\quad \beta_k=\frac{\langle g_{k+1},v_{k+1}\rangle}{\langle g_k,v_k\rangle},\quad p_{k+1}=-v_{k+1}+\beta_kp_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an initial point, PCG forms the gradient, applies the fixed preconditioner, and repeatedly updates the iterate, gradient, preconditioned gradient, and conjugate search direction using the displayed alpha and beta coefficients.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Energy-norm convergence bound for preconditioned conjugate gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric PCG error bound in the energy norm, controlled by the spectral condition number of the preconditioned SPD system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0, M=M^{\mathsf T}\succ0, x_*=-H^{-1}c, and \epsilon_k=x_k-x_* for the iterates of preconditioned conjugate gradient. If \epsilon_0\ne0, then \frac{\|\epsilon_k\|_H}{\|\epsilon_0\|_H}\le 2\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa(M^{-1}H)}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa(M^{-1}H)}+1}\right)^k, where \|z\|_H=\sqrt{z^{\mathsf T}Hz} and \kappa(M^{-1}H) denotes the spectral condition number.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For PCG on an SPD quadratic, the relative error in the H-energy norm is bounded by twice the kth power of the standard contraction factor determined by the spectral condition number of the preconditioned matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Memoryless BFGS representation and exact-line-search equivalence with Hestenes–Stiefel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric representation of nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions, including the failed naive symmetrization and the exact-line-search equivalence boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\), and \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\). The Hestenes--Stiefel direction can be written
\[
p_{k+1}=-\widehat H_{k+1}g_{k+1},\qquad \widehat H_{k+1}=I-\frac{s_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}.
\]
The matrix \(\widehat H_{k+1}\) is generally neither symmetric nor positive definite. Moreover, \(\widehat H_{k+1}^T\widehat H_{k+1}\) is singular and does not in general satisfy the secant equation. If \(y_k^Ts_k>0\), the one-pair inverse-BFGS matrix
\[
H_{k+1}=\left(I-\frac{s_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}\right)\left(I-\frac{y_ks_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}\right)+\frac{s_ks_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}
\]
is symmetric positive definite and satisfies \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\). It is obtained by one inverse-BFGS update of \(I\), so resetting to \(I\) and retaining only \((s_k,y_k)\) gives memoryless BFGS, equivalently L-BFGS with \(m=1\) and identity initialization. Under exact line searches, which give \(g_{k+1}^Tp_k=0\),
\[
-H_{k+1}g_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\frac{g_{k+1}^Ty_k}{y_k^Tp_k}p_k,
\]
so memoryless BFGS produces the Hestenes--Stiefel direction; with the resulting conjugate-gradient orthogonality, the Hestenes--Stiefel coefficient also reduces to the Polak--Ribiere coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct matrix representation of the Hestenes–Stiefel direction is generally nonsymmetric, while its naive Gram symmetrization is singular and fails the secant equation. A single inverse-BFGS update of the identity supplies a symmetric positive-definite secant matrix when the curvature product is positive. Retaining only this newest pair gives memoryless BFGS, and under exact line searches its direction equals Hestenes–Stiefel and consequently the corresponding Polak–Ribiere form.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at the iterates in question, \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\), and \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\).
\(y_k^Ts_k>0\) for the symmetric positive-definite inverse-BFGS conclusion.
For equivalence with nonlinear conjugate gradient, the line searches are exact, giving the required direction-gradient orthogonality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Memoryless BFGS}=\text{L-BFGS}(m=1,H^0=I),\qquad p_{k+1}=p_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HS}}\text{ under exact line searches, with the corresponding HS coefficient reducing to PR.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate-transformed preconditioned nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction representations obtained by applying a nonlinear conjugate-gradient update after a nonsingular coordinate transformation, together with a memoryless-BFGS alternative and the absence of a universal preconditioner choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a chosen nonsingular matrix \(C\), let \(W=C^TC\), \(x=C^{-1}z\), and \(\widetilde f(z)=f(C^{-1}z)\). Define \(z_k=Cx_k\), \(\widetilde g_k=C^{-T}g_k\), \(\widetilde d_k=Cd_k\), \(\widetilde s_k=Cs_k\), and \(\widetilde y_k=C^{-T}y_k\). Applying the displayed conjugate-gradient update in the transformed coordinates yields
\[
d_{k+1}=-\left(I-\frac{d_ky_k^T}{d_k^Ty_k}\right)W^{-1}g_{k+1}.
\]
A corresponding preconditioned memoryless-BFGS direction is
\[
d_{k+1}=-\left[I-\frac{y_ks_k^T+s_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}+\left(1+\frac{y_k^Ty_k}{y_k^Ts_k}\right)\frac{s_ks_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k}\right]W^{-1}g_{k+1}.
\]
For nonquadratic minimization, the preconditioning matrix may be chosen differently from one iteration to another; its selection is problem dependent, and no general-purpose preconditioner formula is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular coordinate transformation with W = C^T C converts the displayed nonlinear conjugate-gradient update into a preconditioned direction in the original variables. The extract also gives a preconditioned memoryless-BFGS direction. In nonquadratic minimization, the preconditioner may vary by iteration, but its choice depends on the problem and has no general-purpose formula.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is differentiable at the iterates under consideration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_{k+1}=-\left(I-\frac{d_ky_k^T}{d_k^Ty_k}\right)W^{-1}g_{k+1},\quad\text{or the stated memoryless-BFGS alternative; the preconditioner may vary by iteration and has no universal problem-independent formula.}

children.title: Conjugacy Under Metric Changes
children.top_down_role: Effects of scaling or metric variation on direction quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugacy Under Metric Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact preservation criterion for pairwise conjugacy when the defining metric changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k,M_{k+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive-definite matrices and define \(\langle u,v\rangle_{M}=u^{\mathsf T}Mv\). If two nonzero directions \(d_i,d_j\) are conjugate in metric \(M_k\), so \(d_i^{\mathsf T}M_kd_j=0\), then they remain conjugate in metric \(M_{k+1}\) if and only if \[d_i^{\mathsf T}(M_{k+1}-M_k)d_j=0.\] Consequently, arbitrary positive-definite metric changes need not preserve previously established conjugacy; preservation requires the metric perturbation to vanish on every relevant cross-pair of stored directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directions conjugate in one metric remain conjugate after a metric change exactly when the metric perturbation has zero cross-product on those directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_i^{\mathsf T}M_{k+1}d_j=0\) if and only if \(d_i^{\mathsf T}(M_{k+1}-M_k)d_j=0\).

notation.meaning: Inner product induced by a positive-definite matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Wolfe Globalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-Wolfe line search applied to nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<c_1<c_2<1\). Given \(x_k\), gradient \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and a descent direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) such that \[f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\] and \[\left|\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k\right|\leq c_2\left|g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\right|.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), compute the selected nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficient, and form the next direction; restart with \(-g_{k+1}\) whenever the proposed direction is not descent. Stop at the prescribed gradient tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong-Wolfe globalization accepts a step only when sufficient decrease and absolute curvature conditions hold, with restart if the next conjugate-gradient direction is not descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted step satisfies both strong-Wolfe inequalities before the nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence continues.

children.title: Sufficient-Descent Modifications

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient-Descent Modifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fallback modification enforcing uniform descent in nonlinear conjugate-gradient iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), an iterate \(x_k\), gradient \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), previous direction \(d_{k-1}\), tentative coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\), and constant \(c\in(0,1]\), form \(\widehat d_k=-g_k+\widehat\beta_k d_{k-1}\). Set \[d_k=\begin{cases}\widehat d_k,&g_k^{\mathsf T}\widehat d_k\le -c\lVert g_k\rVert^2,\\-g_k,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\] Choose a positive line-search step \(\alpha_k\) and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\). Stop when a prescribed gradient tolerance is met. Every accepted direction satisfies \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept the conjugate-gradient direction only when it provides uniform sufficient descent; otherwise restart with steepest descent.

children.title: Conjugate-Gradient Restart Trigger Family
children.top_down_role: Scheduled and geometry-triggered returns to steepest descent.

children.title: Periodic Conjugate-Gradient Restarts
children.top_down_role: Scheduled returns to steepest-descent directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Conjugate-Gradient Restarts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-frequency restart rule for nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer period \(m\ge1\). Initialize \(d_0=-g_0\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). For each \(k\ge1\), compute a tentative coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\) and set \[\beta_k=\begin{cases}0,&k\equiv0\pmod m,\\\widehat\beta_k,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad d_k=-g_k+\beta_k d_{k-1}.\] Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by the prescribed line search and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Thus every index divisible by \(m\) uses \(d_k=-g_k\), and no block of \(m\) consecutive generated directions contains fewer than one scheduled restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set the conjugacy coefficient to zero every fixed number of iterations, thereby periodically replacing the recurrence by steepest descent.
